cal.title: Fix the timing of the recordings
cal.intro: Between the band leaving the speakers and your guitar reaching the computer there is a small delay. This test measures it once; after that the app corrects every take by itself.
cal.step1: Mute the strings with your fretting hand: resting on them, not pressing.
cal.step2: Click Start. You will hear 8 clicks, a bit more than half a second apart.
cal.step3: Strum the muted strings together with each click ("chk"), firmly.
cal.no_input: No audio input was found. Connect the interface (e.g. the GT-100) and choose it in the "Input" menu at the top.
cal.current: Current setting: {ms} ms. You can measure again whenever you like (for example after changing the sound output).
cal.not_done: Not done yet. It takes about 10 seconds.
cal.failed_tip: Strum the muted strings firmly, together with each click, and click Start again.
cal.result: The recordings arrived {ms} ms {side}; from now on they land on time. ({hits} of {clicks} strums measured.)
cal.spread: Your strums varied a lot (±{ms} ms). If you like, repeat with firmer strums.

help.title: What each thing is
help.now: The chord that is sounding, with the degree (I, IV, ♭VII…: the distance to the main note of the song) and the shape on the neck. Below, the beats of the bar, each split in 3 (in 12/8: count "1-and-a, 2-and-a…") or in 2 (in 4/4: "1-and, 2-and…"). On the right, the next chord and how many beats until it, the section of the song and the bar.
help.timeline: A click: goes to the start of that bar. Drag: marks a part to loop. Double-click a section of the song (top lane): loops that whole section. The edges of the loop can be dragged.
help.band: Each instrument has an on/off button and a volume. "You will play" turns off the right part with one click and sets where the recording goes. When you have takes, each part can play the original or yours.
help.record: Press Record (or R): the count-in comes, the band plays and your guitar is recorded from the input chosen at the top (the GT-100 or another interface). Press again (or Space) to stop. Each recording becomes a take, already aligned with the band. With the loop on, it records one pass and stops by itself.
help.takes: ▶ plays the take in place of the original, with the band. ★ marks the good ones. In the ⋯ menu: analyze the timing (where you rushed or dragged, bar by bar), fix the timing of the take by ear, export MP3, rename and delete (it can be undone).
help.meter: The level of the guitar reaching the computer. Green is good. Yellow or gray: low (raise the output volume of the pedalboard or the gain of the interface; on the GT-100, the PATCH LEVEL). Red: clipping (lower it).
help.devices: Input: where the guitar comes from. With the GT-100 connected, the app picks it by itself; for another interface, choose it in the menu. Output: where the band plays, on the computer speakers or on the interface itself (together with the guitar, in the headphones or the amp).
help.songs: In the songs menu, Import a song turns an MP3 into a practice song with the local AI: it separates the instruments, finds the beats and the bars and suggests the chords (correct them in chords.txt). Add a music folder adds a folder with songs already separated (one folder per song, with drums, bass, vocals...).
help.lyrics: The Lyrics button (key K) shows the lyrics next to the band. With Follow on, the line being sung lights up a moment early and the lyrics scroll by themselves; off, it is just the text, to read. Click a line to play from it. The lyrics come from you: paste them, or leave an .lrc file (lyrics with the time of each line) in the song folder, and Riffroom lines it up with the voice of the song. Without times, use ⋯ > Mark the times while it plays.
help.ai: Riffroom can be driven by an AI assistant such as Claude (Claude Desktop or Claude Code), through MCP. Ask, for example, "open the demo song, loop the solo and record three takes" and then "where did I rush?". The installer registers it; nothing of your audio leaves the computer.
help.k_home: back to the start (or to the start of the loop)
help.k_modes: you will play: the buttons of the Band panel, in order
tour.modes.title: Choose what you will play
tour.modes.text: Click the part you will play (for example "Rhythm guitar"): the app turns that part of the band off, and the recording goes into it. "Just listen" turns everything on.
tour.play.title: Play along
tour.play.text: Press Play (or Space). Before the music moves, the count-in gives 4 beats: come in on the next ONE. A click on the timeline goes to another bar; dragging marks a part to loop.
tour.now.title: Follow the NOW panel
tour.now.text: It shows the chord that is sounding, the degree and the shape on the neck. The dots are the beats of the bar, each split in equal parts: count along, the way it is written below them.
tour.record.title: Record and compare
tour.record.text: Press Record (or R) and play; press again to stop. The take shows up in "Your takes", already aligned: ▶ plays yours in place of the original, and ⋯ > Analyze the timing shows where you rushed or dragged.
tour.calibrate.title: Before the first recording
tour.calibrate.text: Check the Input at the top (where your guitar comes from) and do "Fix the timing" once (about 10 seconds). It measures the delay of the computer, and the recordings start landing right on time.
